text:
prod_incident_bot: INCIDENT OPENED · SEV: P1 · us-east-1a networking slowpath impacting inference pools. Alerts: 65% of g5 instances reporting RX errors / high kernel drops. Trigger: net-metrics threshold cross. Paging oncall-ec2.

oncall-ec2: got the page, i'm oncall — joining now. spinning up tmate.

sre_jamie: i'm on call too, starting quick triage. checking ENI error counters and instance-level dmesg. seen earlier similar pattern to partial host NIC firmware flaps.

eng_runtime_laura: seeing token latency spikes and 503s from router -> runtime path, 95th latency jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s for a subset of requests. KV cache misses up 40%. logs: ```2023-11-08T12:01:23Z router WARN dial tcp i/o timeout -> conn reset```

infra-bot: runbook: https://internal/runbooks/az-net-slowpath. Recommended immediate actions: 1) move critical traffic away from affected AZ, 2) reduce DNS TTL for api.redwood-inference, 3) spawn replacement instances in healthy AZs.

oncall-ec2: starting AZ-level traffic steering. lowering DNS TTL to 30s as quick measure. adding route policy to prefer us-east-1b/1c for inference routes.

cust_success_mark: FYI two support cases opened in last 5m (CS-4521, CS-4522) — multiple customers report request timeouts and retries. one enterprise reported 15% error rate for inference calls. they want ETA.

sre_jamie: copying CS update: working mitigation — steering traffic off us-east-1a, standing up replacement g5 nodes in 1b, will keep customers posted.

eng_platform_zoe: adding fallback model routing: for timeouts we can route to a smaller quantized variant in healthy AZs to reduce tail latency while instances join. enabling canary fallback now (route weight 10% -> 50%). pls monitor quality regressions.

sre_ops_ali: i'll run host-level checks on instances in us-east-1a. initial `ethtool -S` shows RX errors spiking on eni-09f4. collecting pcap on a subset.

eng_runtime_laura: note — moving traffic will cause KV cache cold starts. suggest warmup probe after routing shift: run `/probe warmup --model gpt-medium --requests 200` against new pool.

prod_incident_bot: NOTE: automated failover to dedicated standby pool not enabled for this customer cohort. manual routing changes in progress.

oncall-ec2: DNS TTL lowered. ALB weights adjusted to prefer 1b/1c. spinning up 6 replacement g5 nodes in us-east-1b (requested from infra autoscaler).

sre_jamie: observed drop in error rate after initial weight shift (~10m). p50 latency recovering, p95 still elevated ~600ms. continuing monitoring.

cust_success_mark: sent interim note to affected customers: "we're routing traffic to healthy AZs and provisioning replacements, will follow up with timeline and postmortem." responses so far neutral, one asked for failover SLA details.

eng_platform_zoe: increased canary fallback to 40% to reduce tail for customer-facing endpoints while new instances warm. starting warmup probes now.

sre_ops_ali: kernel logs show NIC resets on a subset of hosts, suspect vendor-level control plane issue in the AZ. opening a cloud provider ticket (Vendor-Ticket-99824) and attaching pcap and counters.

infra-bot: cloud provider status check: us-east-1a reported increased network plane retries in last 30m; provider investigating. link: https://status.aws.example/incident/99824 (internal).

eng_runtime_laura: after warmup we see KV cache hit-rate improving and 503s dropping. still tracking a few sticky sessions that hit old nodes — draining them now. command: ```kubectl cordon node-az1a-09 && kubectl drain node-az1a-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

non-technical_note: staging of customer-facing metrics dashboard updated to show degraded availability and model latency per-tenant.

cust_success_mark: pushing a follow-up to customers with timeline: "initial mitigation completed, full recovery expected within 1h pending provider remediation. we'll post updates and a postmortem."

prod_incident_bot: SEVERITY DOWNGRADE PROPOSAL: from P1 -> P2 if error rate < 2% for 15m. currently error rate 1.8% over last 10m.

sre_jamie: holding until cloud vendor acknowledges root cause; but ok to downgrade to P2 if trend continues.

eng_platform_zoe: created temporary routing policy so customers with SLAs are pinned to multi-AZ pools to avoid single-AZ exposure in future. added followup ticket to infra backlog: IR-2376 (enable automatic multi-AZ failover for hosted API).

sre_ops_ali: vendor confirmed hardware-level NIC controller retries in us-east-1a, mitigation in progress on their side. they estimate 2-3 hours for full remediation. we have our traffic steered and replacement hosts out of the AZ; customer impact minimal now.

on-technical_note2: handoff: @sre_jamie handing off to @sre_ops_ali for vendor liaison and watch. i will prepare incident timeline and start postmortem doc.

sre_ops_ali: acknowledged, taking lead. will keep channel updated.

prod_incident_bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated (traffic steered, replacement hosts healthy). severity: P2. incident channel will remain open for vendor remediation and postmortem coordination.

eng_runtime_laura: quick action items added to postmortem: 1) enable multi-AZ automatic routing for host pools, 2) failover test runbook, 3) reduce TTL on health check changes, 4) consider model-variant fallback automation.

cust_success_mark: flagged customers for follow-up and scheduled a sync with account teams.

sre_jamie: thanks all. closing shift. will draft timeline and root cause in postmortem doc and link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
